skill.name: react-components
skill.description: Converts Stitch screens into modular Vite and React components with Tailwind token mapping and SWC validation.
skill.summary: Generate modular React components from Stitch designs with validation guidance.
skill.author: google-labs-code

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, JSX template literals, Apache license URLs, and ordinary relative imports. The confirmed risks are the intentional Bash and npm workflow, an unconstrained curl download helper, and validator file reads from CLI-supplied paths. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The fetch helper accepts any URL and output path.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only expected Stitch or Google Cloud Storage HTTPS hosts, reject absolute or parent output paths, and write only under a temporary workspace directory.

remediation.issue: The skill grants broad Bash, Write, Read, and web_fetch permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed tools where possible, or require explicit user confirmation before network fetches, package installation, dev server startup, or file writes.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs npm install and project npm scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer pinned dependencies and a lockfile, document script execution clearly, and require confirmation before installing packages or starting a server.

remediation.issue: The validator reads a path provided on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths against the workspace, reject paths outside source directories, and fail cleanly when no component path is provided.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs agents to run a Bash helper with htmlCode.downloadUrl, and scripts/fetch-stitch.sh passes URL and OUTPUT arguments directly to curl. The helper lacks scheme, domain, and output path restrictions.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools block explicitly grants broad execution, file, and network capabilities. This is not malicious by itself, but it expands the trust boundary for a community skill.

content.user_title: Convert Stitch Designs to React Components
content.value_statement: Turning Stitch designs into maintainable React code can be slow and inconsistent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through retrieval, component structure, token mapping, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Uses Stitch MCP screen metadata and signed download URLs as design inputs.
Downloads Stitch HTML through a provided curl helper when normal fetch tools fail.
Scaffolds modular React and Vite components from a TypeScript template.
Maps Tailwind theme values against the included style guide.
Runs SWC-based validation for props interfaces and hardcoded hex colors.
Guides separation of components, hooks, mock data, and app wiring.
limitations: Requires access to a working Stitch MCP server and valid screen metadata.
Uses Bash and curl, so restricted environments may need approval.
Validation checks only props interfaces and hardcoded hex colors.
Generated components still need visual review in the target application.

prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [screen] into React components and map colors, spacing, and fonts to my project Tailwind theme. Avoid hardcoded hex values.

prompt_templates.title: Build Component System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced conversion with data and logic separation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [flow] into a component system. Separate mock data, hooks, reusable components, and app wiring before running validation.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Generated UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after an initial conversion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the generated React components against the architecture checklist. Fix structure, props typing, theme mapping, and validation failures.

output_examples.input: Convert a Stitch activity feed card into React.
output: A reusable activity card component with typed props.
Mock content moved into a separate data layer.
Validation notes for props structure and color usage.

output_examples.input: Create a Vite component system from a Stitch dashboard screen.
output: A set of smaller dashboard components organized by responsibility.
Theme mapping guidance for colors, typography, and spacing.
A checklist summary for structure, validation, and visual review.

output_examples.input: Review generated components for architecture issues.
output: A concise list of missing props, hardcoded styles, and oversized files.
Suggested fixes that preserve the project structure.
A final validation status for each reviewed component.

best_practices: Confirm the Stitch screen, viewport, and project theme before generating files.
Review every network fetch and command before allowing the workflow to run.
Run visual checks after validation because AST checks cannot verify layout fidelity.
anti_patterns: Do not paste untrusted design URLs into Bash commands without review.
Do not keep large generated screens as single React files.
Do not treat validation success as proof of visual accuracy.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps convert Stitch screens into modular React and Vite components with Tailwind token guidance.

faq.question: Does it require Stitch MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects Stitch MCP metadata, including screen HTML and screenshot download URLs.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run Bash, npm install, npm validation, and a local dev server command.

faq.question: What validation is included?
faq.answer: The validator parses TypeScript with SWC and checks for props interfaces and hardcoded hex colors.

faq.question: Can it build a complete app?
faq.answer: It focuses on generated component structure and app wiring. Product logic and final UX review remain separate work.

faq.question: Is it safe in locked-down environments?
faq.answer: It may need extra approval because it uses network fetches, filesystem writes, and local command execution.
